texts.preamble: Smt. Bathini Chitrakala vs The State Of Telangana on 12 June, 2023 Author: K.Lakshman Bench: K.Lakshman, P.Sree Sudha Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman And Hon'Ble Smt. Justice P. Sree Sudha Writ Petition No.11787 of 2023 Order:
texts.facts: Petitioner herein is the wife of the detenu i.e., Bathini Thirupathi has filed this writ petition. 3. Perusal of record would reveal that the detenu, the petitioner's husband is a delivery boy in Samruddi Indane Gas Agency, Waddepalli, Hanmankonda. Two crimes were registered against him. Crime No.222 of 2022 of P.S. Manakondur was registered against the KL,J & PSS,J W.P. No.11787_2023 detenu on 09.10.2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 457, 380 of IPC and Section 25(1)(a) of Arms Act. The allegations against the detenu are that he has committing theft of 140 full and 140 empty gas cylinders from gas godown of the said firm. The aforesaid case was registered on the complaint lodged by the Managing Partner of the aforesaid firm. 4. Crime No.293 of 2022 was registered by Karimnagar I Town Police Station against the detenu on 09.11.2022 on the complaint lodged by Managing Partner of the aforesaid firm for the offences punishable under Sections 452, 392 and 307 of IPC and Section 25(1)(a) of Arms Act. The allegation against the detenu in the said complaint was extortion of money i.e., Rs.34,875/- by showing fire arms. 5. According to learned Special Government Pleader, the Investigating Officer in both the crimes have already completed investigation and filed charge sheets against the detenu and the same were taken on file and assigned calendar case numbers which are pending before the trial Court. The allegations leveled against the detenu are serious, disturbed the public order. Considering the nature KL,J & PSS,J W.P. No.11787_2023 of offences, the manner in which, they were committed by the detenu, material on record, respondent No.2 passed detention order and confirmed by respondent Smt. Bathini Chitrakala vs The State Of Telangana on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164436788/ 1 No.1. There is no irregularity.
texts.arguments: 6. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1, the Apex Court held as under: "...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some? The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them. Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder. Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder. When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder. It will thus appear that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order". It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State." 7. In Banka Sneha Sheela v. State of Telangana2, the Apex Court held as under: 13. There can be no doubt that for 'public order' to be disturbed, there must in turn be public disorder. Mere contravention of law such as indulging in cheating or criminal breach of trust certainly affects 'law and order' but before it can be said to affect 'public order', it must affect the community or the public at large." The impugned judgment is [LEAKAGE_MASK] and the Detenu is ordered to be freed forthwith. In Mallada K. Sri Ram v. The State of Telangana3, the Apex Court held that a mere apprehension of a breach of law and order is not sufficient to meet the standard of adversely affecting the "maintenance of public order". Referring to the principle laid down by it in Ram Manohar Lohia3 and Banka Sneha Sheela5, the distinction between a disturbance to law and order and a disturbance to public order was discussed. Similar view was reiterated by Apex Court in Shaik Nazneen v. The State of Telangana4. 9.
